Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: first-person point-and-click castle exploration game background. Output ONE full-bleed landscape 1536x1024 image, 3:2, no collage. Fine realistic painted environmental concept art for the SAME inhabited medium-sized western fantasy lord's castle: pale warm-gray limestone ashlar masonry and restrained pointed arches, textured dark oak beams and doors, muted wine-red cloth, small aged bronze fittings. Crisp legible architectural edges, realistic material texture, straight rigid construction and coherent perspective. Spacious and dignified domestic castle scale, approximately 3.8m ceiling for these corridors. Soft cool daylight with restrained warm candle accents, luminous natural colors, welcoming lived-in calm. Standing eye-level view, natural broad field of view, clear foreground to middle distance, level floor. No people, no text, no signs, no UI, no arrows, no glowing outlines, no emblems, no watermark, no modern objects, no exaggerated palace or cathedral scale, no open balcony overlooking a lower floor. Do not draw the return navigation icon: it is added by the frontend.
Scene: the UPPER GUEST-WING CORRIDOR, separate from the existing lord's private corridor. Camera has just passed through the closed dark-oak single pointed door from the upper stair landing; that doorway is BEHIND the camera and not visible. An inviting comfortable corridor with a short clear sightline and subdued red runner on level flagstones. EXACTLY TWO navigable openings visible: (1) A complete CLOSED dark-oak pointed guest-room door in the near LEFT wall, approximately x=12%-33%, y=16%-91%, frame, ring handle and threshold completely exposed. (2) A generously sized OPEN pointed stone doorway at the FAR RIGHT OF CENTER, approximately x=57%-76%, y=25%-82%, leading into an enclosed tower stairwell. Through this tower doorway show only the first few rigid rectangular upward stone treads and a solid stone return wall hiding the continuation; no spiral staircase, no warped fan-shaped steps, no exterior landscape through this opening. The tower entrance must be visibly separate from the guest-room door and reached directly from the corridor, without crossing any bedroom. The right-hand wall has a tall leaded window admitting soft cool light and a modest built-in window seat with a simple muted-red cushion; these are solid glazed windows, not extra exit arches. A sober oak ceiling, pale limestone and small bronze wall sconces tie the guest wing to the existing upper landing. Keep the central walking line and both door silhouettes unobstructed. The corridor should feel quieter and more intimate than the great hall; no row of extra doors, no distant tiny doors, no gallery balcony, no lower floor, no magical effects. No extra navigable opening.
